title: When the Wreck Wakes
premise: Beatrix Marchetti, a railroad engineer who has spent twelve years mapping closed lines to outrun a grief he refuses to name, is hired to survey a coastal route when a winter storm strips away the cliff face and exposes a sea cave that local legend says swallowed an entire expedition in 1911. Inside, Beatrix and the ragtag crew he reluctantly leads — a disgraced archivist, a teenage stowaway, and the widow of the man whose death Beatrix has hidden for twelve years — find not treasure but the expedition's intact records, which prove the railway company deliberately sealed the cave and buried its own dead to protect a land deal. As the tide rises and the company's fixers close in, Beatrix must choose between loyalty to his crew and the truth that could destroy them all, and in the end he chooses truth: he confesses his own buried secret at the cave mouth, the group escapes with the records as the sea reclaims the passage, and the found family they've become carries the story into daylight.
about_author: Casper Vasquez is the pen name of a former surveyor's assistant who spent six years walking abandoned rail grades along the Pacific coast before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about people who measure their lives in distances rather than dates.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Beatrix Marchetti's POV. Twelve years after a tunnel collapse he survived and his best friend didn't, Beatrix measures life in track miles, taking a lonely contract to survey a decommissioned coastal line. A winter storm batters the cliffs. The emotional beat is controlled numbness cracking at the edges as the sea does something impossible overnight.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The storm has sheared away the cliff face, revealing a cave mouth and, wedged in the rock, a rusted lantern stamped with the date 1911. Local legend names it the Wreck Cave, where a survey expedition vanished. Beatrix reports it — and is stunned when the railway company offers him triple pay to lead a recovery team immediately. Beat: dread disguised as opportunity.

chapters.title: A Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Beatrix and Odile Ferrand, a disgraced corporate archivist assigned to the team. They assemble: Odile, taciturn diver Tomas Reyes, and fifteen-year-old stowaway Juniper Hale, discovered hiding in the supply car. Beatrix wants to send her back; she has nowhere to go. Beat: reluctant bonds forming under pressure, each member hiding something.

chapters.title: The Widow on the Platform
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the last station before the coast, Mara Voss boards uninvited — the widow of Daniel Voss, the friend who died in Beatrix's tunnel. She has spent twelve years asking questions Beatrix has dodged, and she suspects this cave connects to her husband's final letter. Beat: guilt made flesh; Beatrix realizes he cannot control this story much longer.

chapters.title: Into the Dark That Keeps Its Dead
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The team enters the cave at low tide, racing the water table. They find the 1911 expedition's camp preserved: journals, instruments, and bones arranged with care. The journals hint the party didn't die by accident — someone sealed the entrance from outside. Beat: wonder curdling into fear; the cave is a crime scene.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Deciphering the records, Odile discovers the 1911 expedition found rich mineral seams; the railway's founders murdered them and collapsed the entrance to claim the land cheaply — the same fraud pattern Beatrix's own tunnel collapse fits. Odile confronts Beatrix privately. Beat: two keepers of secrets recognizing each other, trust forged in complicity.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A 'safety inspection' team arrives — actually company fixers ordered to recover and destroy the records, and if necessary the witnesses. Juniper, eavesdropping, warns the others, but the fixers seize the entrance equipment and strand the team inside as the tide turns. Beat: betrayal, panic, and Juniper stepping up from stowaway to savior.

chapters.title: Rising Water, Rising Truth
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Trapped deep in the cave with water climbing, Beatrix must use his engineer's knowledge of old drainage adits to find an escape route — and Mara forces the issue of his secret, demanding truth before anyone moves. He confesses: the tunnel collapse was caused by his ignored safety report, and Daniel died covering for him. Beat: the climax of guilt; honesty as survival.

chapters.title: The Adit
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The team floods the record chamber behind them to stop the fixers, then navigates the forgotten drainage adit Beatrix maps from memory and instinct. Tomas is nearly lost saving the journals; Juniper pulls him out. They surface at dawn through a ventilation shaft above the cliff. Beat: sacrifice, teamwork, the found family holding under maximum strain.

chapters.title: Open Line
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, epilogue tone. The records go public; the company's heirs are exposed, and the 1911 dead are named and buried properly. Beatrix testifies about his own tunnel, surrendering his license but keeping his integrity. Mara stays; Odile, Tomas, and Juniper become something like family. The sea has reclaimed the cave. Final beat: Beatrix finally measures life in years — and plans to spend them with these people.
